covers.quote: Only create content that meets a need.
Only design and write content that meets a real person’s need.

rules.quote: Create content that meets a real need
rules.specification: Assessing this requires information about actual users and their needs. The page does not provide a text-only test for whether a need is real or has been met.
rules.violation_condition: Content that does not meet a real person’s need.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading and its restatements; G-5 excludes the separate instructions about conducting research.

covers.quote: This includes other people working in government as well as end users.

examples.note: This illustrates the research and review process, rather than presenting an actual compliant report passage.

parts.quote: You are a policy officer working on a short progress report for a senior manager. The report updates the manager on a government policy your team is developing.
As you write the report you check for assumptions about the people the policy will affect. You identify some untested assumptions so you raise this with the team for more research.

rules.quote: If you are writing about other people, make sure you are not making assumptions about them.
rules.specification: Determining whether a statement rests on an untested assumption requires information about its evidential basis; the wording alone may not establish a violation.
rules.violation_condition: Statements about other people that rest on untested assumptions.
when: Applies when writing about other people, including people working in government and end users.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the different groups of people within one check; G-5 separates the restriction on assumptions in writing from the surrounding research-process advice.
